value: Six captured indexed Custom Endpoints pages are the bounded reference packet, not proof of complete vendor or Console API equivalence. Beta availability does not remove explicitly requested custom endpoint capability.

Only unrestricted Developer Console applications are documented as supported; the same page instructs configuring backing resource access restrictions. This public ambiguity must remain visible. Console requires scoped application authority intersected with current resource/field/Action/function policy and never exposes unrestricted credentials to user code.

Endpoint-set edit/view/publish/deploy authority differs from executing its backing resource. Folder permission inheritance is a vendor illustration, not a replacement for Console Group/Company and Cedar enforcement.

All parameters including optional ones require mapping; certain JSON values are body-only. GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH are listed, but no exhaustive type/location compatibility table is published in these six pages. Unsupported mapping combinations require explicit errors and reviewed local type oracles.

Overview promises response-shape/specification customization; detailed pages document request mapping but do not specify an exhaustive response transformation grammar, error/status mapping, or OpenAPI export. Keep those support dimensions unresolved rather than inventing vendor semantics.

User-defined method remapping does not authorize unsafe GET mutations, weaker preflight/execute validation, missing CSRF/idempotency controls, or another writer. Consequential requests invoke canonical typed commands and preserve receipts; classical user functions execute outside trusted Console.

Publishing creates immutable semantic-version snapshots; tagging without deployment must remain possible. Deleting a vendor release does not authorize deleting Console audit/history, historical command bytes, custody fingerprints, or retention/legal-hold-protected artifacts.

An omitted version selects latest deployed in the reference; Console execution must record the resolved immutable version and backing dependencies. Historical retries must not silently resolve against a later release, and rollback must preserve completed-effect reconciliation.

Custom domain registration/approval and endpoint deployment are separate from publication. Local implementation/testing remains permitted before domain approval. Live domain/DNS/TLS/exposure decisions remain separately authorized; this research grants none.

Documentation uses generated bearer tokens and OAuth-backed apps, but does not specify complete scopes, token revocation/cache timing, streaming, CORS, limits, cancellation, or ambiguous response recovery; exact support and acceptance remain unbound.
Reference mappings describe native Console-equivalent functionality only; no Palantir SDK/API dependency or vendor import/export compatibility is asserted.
